t2i_prompt: A wide web page section on a deep navy background drawn as an engineering sheet with zone letters, a revision block top right and a title block bottom right. A light sans-serif headline with a small qualifier line sits top left. Below, a clean square-cornered table with hairline row rules and muted column headers holds <CONTENT>. A thin steel-blue pipe line enters from an intake chevron on the left edge and runs around the table, passing small isometric pale blue-white hairline equipment drawings placed in the margins, with dimension lines and dotted flow arrows. Flat, no shading, no people.
signature_idea: A plain budget table turned into a drawing by wrapping it in the water path, with each piece of equipment parked beside the row it prices.
strengths: very readable table; numbers are the hero, which suits procurement
qualifier line (currency, date, estimate class) is a credible spec-sheet habit
margin equipment adds context without crowding the data
simple to build from existing table component plus SVG frame
weaknesses: the pipe frame is decorative; it does not map clearly to rows
figures not in monospace, so columns do not align like a spec sheet
equipment placement does not consistently match row order
invented prices in the image are not real data
brand_fit_why: Navy, hairlines, square table, one steel-blue line and calm data-first layout fit the brand; missing Geist Mono figures and limestone relief.
